title: Brain Dissection Protocol
author: Ana Catarina Carapinha Cascalho
materials: Ensure all tools and materials are sterilized.
Wear appropriate personal protective equipment like a lab coat and gloves.
Lift the brain out of the skull gently.

steps.title: Prepare clean workspace
steps.instruction: Set up a clean and organized workspace before beginning the dissection.

steps.title: Euthanize via cervical dislocation
steps.instruction: Perform cervical dislocation without using anesthesia to minimize anesthesia‑related effects.

steps.title: Remove head with scissors
steps.instruction: Using surgical scissors, cut posterior to the ears to remove the head.

steps.title: Make midline skin incision
steps.instruction: Make a midline incision in the skin using scissors.

steps.title: Expose skull by reflecting skin
steps.instruction: Flip the skin over the eyes to fully expose the skull.

steps.title: Incise skull with Iris scissors
steps.instruction: With Iris scissors, make a small incision on the top of the skull starting at the caudal interparietal bone; avoid cutting through brain tissue.

steps.title: Cut anterior frontal bone
steps.instruction: Make a firm cut through the most anterior part of the skull between the eyes (frontal bone) to facilitate easier brain removal.

steps.title: Remove parietal bones
steps.instruction: Tilt one side of the parietal bone with curved narrow‑pattern forceps and break it off; repeat for the opposite side.

substeps.instruction: Tilt one side of the parietal bone with curved narrow‑pattern forceps.
Repeat the procedure for the other side.

steps.title: Remove remaining frontal bone
steps.instruction: If any frontal bone remains, make a small incision to facilitate its removal, taking care not to damage the meninges between brain and skull.

steps.title: Detach brain with forceps
steps.instruction: Slide the closed curved narrow‑pattern forceps under the anterior part of the brain (olfactory bulb), gently tilt upward to lift the brain, then slide further down to break optic and other cranial nerves, freeing the brain from the meninges.

substeps.instruction: Slide closed curved narrow‑pattern forceps under the anterior brain (olfactory bulb).
Gently tilt the forceps upward to lift the brain.
Slide the forceps further down to break optic and other cranial nerves.

steps.title: Wash brain in ice‑cold DPBS
steps.instruction: Wash the extracted brain thoroughly with ice‑cold DPBS (Sigma; D8662) placed on a gelatin plate.

steps.title: Separate brain hemispheres
steps.instruction: Cut the brain into left and right hemispheres.

steps.title: Dissect regions of interest
steps.instruction: Dissect the following areas from each hemisphere as needed: cerebellum, cortex, interbrain, hindbrain.

steps.title: Place tissue in labeled tubes
steps.instruction: Place each dissected brain part into pre‑labeled tubes, handling tissues gently to avoid damage.

steps.title: Snap‑freeze and store samples
steps.instruction: Snap‑freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen, then store at –80 °C until further analysis; work quickly to preserve tissue integrity.
